q: The physics describing motion, called ____, was discussed in the previous chapter.
e: The physics describing motion, called kinematics, was discussed in the previous chapter. Kinematics names the physics describing motion, called, was discussed in the previous chapter.

q: This chapter is dealt with ____ which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc.
e: This chapter is dealt with dynamics which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: A fundamental concept in dynamics is ____.
e: A fundamental concept in dynamics is force. Force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: Force is defined precisely by ____.
e: Force is defined precisely by Newton's laws of motion. The physics in this sentence is built around Newton's laws of motion.

q: Force can change the ____ of an object.
e: Force can change the state of motion of an object. The physics in this sentence is built around state of motion.

q: Newton's first law states that: When no ____ acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity.
e: Newton's first law states that: When no net external force acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity. Net external force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: In mathematical form, If ____ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero.
e: In mathematical form, If $F_{net}=0$ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: Newton's first law expresses the idea of ____.
e: Newton's first law expresses the idea of inertia. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: ____ is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion.
e: Inertia is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: In fact, the first law is often referred as the ____.
e: In fact, the first law is often referred as the law of inertia. Law of inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the ____ of particle.
c: product of the mass and the acceleration
e: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the product of the mass and the acceleration of particle. Product of the mass and the acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: In mathematical form, ____
e: In mathematical form, $F_{net}=ma$. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the ____.
e: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the net force. Net force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is ____ to force.
e: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is directly proportional to force. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Therefore, second law is also called ____.
e: Therefore, second law is also called law of force and acceleration. Law of force and acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is ____ to the force exerted by the first on the second.
c: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
e: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force exerted by the first on the second. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies.

q: In other words, for every action, there is an ____.
e: In other words, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. The physics in this sentence is built around equal and opposite reaction.

q: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on ____.
e: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on two separate objects. The physics in this sentence is built around two separate objects.

q: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called 1 newton. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called 1 dyne. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In FPS system the unit of force is ____.
e: In FPS system the unit of force is pound. The unit that belongs with this quantity is pound.

q: The ____ is the unit of mass in British engineering system.
e: The slug is the unit of mass in British engineering system. The unit that belongs with this quantity is slug.
